solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Lose it down a gutter, its front blocking gondola (4,1,6)

indicatorNotes.blocking: the letters block the gondola by sitting inside it

blocks.note: the gondola, or basket, hangs under a hot-air balloon

annotation.surface: Someone loses it, tipping down a gutter while a gondola gets in the way.
annotation.walkthrough: The gondola is the car slung under a hot-air balloon, not the Venetian boat, and 'down' is a mood, not a direction.
annotation.definitionFit: To blow a gasket is to lose your temper explosively, like an engine blowing its seal.

entries.clue: Fastener joins deer and baby animal up (6)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the elk is a large deer
a cub is a young fox, bear or lion

annotation.surface: A fastener somehow joins a deer to a young animal.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer opens with BUCK, which looks like the deer, but it is the tail of the baby animal read upwards; the whole string turns round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the clasp on a belt or strap is the commonest fastener of all.

entries.clue: Mournful and true, I’d a dismal book (3,6,6)

indicatorNotes.dismal: dismal letters are in a sorry state, so they get rearranged

annotation.surface: A gloomy review: the book is sad, honest and dreary.
annotation.walkthrough: Our Mutual Friend is Dickens's last completed novel. Only 'and' is left out of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Our Mutual Friend is a novel by Charles Dickens, so it is a book.

entries.clue: Repairs on inverted cross very near (2,4,4)

indicatorNotes.inverted: inverted means turned upside down, which in a down clue reverses the letters

blocks.note: to atone is to make repair for a wrong
rood is an old word for the cross of Christ

annotation.surface: Someone mends something sitting on an upturned cross nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: Repairs is the verb here, making amends, not the noun for fixes.
annotation.definitionFit: Something at one's door is right on the doorstep, very near.

entries.clue: A modus operandi abroad (4)

blocks.note: Latin for a method of operating: a manner or means of doing something

annotation.surface: A criminal's method of working overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: Modus operandi is usually police jargon for a criminal's habits, which colours the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the travelling sense: a person abroad is not at home but out of the country.

entries.clue: Imperial chief, leader of nation in comfort with uniform on (9)

indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: N goes in the word for comfort
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, on means placed above, so KIT comes first

blocks.note: to cheer someone is to comfort them

annotation.surface: A head of empire, top of the country, relaxing in a uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was the British field marshal of the 'Your country needs you' poster, a chief of the Empire.
annotation.definitionFit: Kitchener commanded imperial forces and was Britain's war minister in 1914.

entries.clue: Success as island blocks top hotel (7)

indicatorNotes.blocks: the island blocks the word for top by lodging in it

blocks.note: to trump is to top or beat
H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A resort wins as an island bars the way to the best hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: Top is a verb, to trump, not the best of something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word began as a Roman general's victory parade and now means any notable win.

entries.clue: Recollection of bread, as fed to natives in wonderful bower? (5,6)

indicatorNotes.Recollection of: re-collection: the bread's letters are collected again in reverse
indicatorNotes.fed to: AS is fed into the natives

blocks.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

annotation.surface: A memory of bread being handed to the locals in a lovely garden arbour.
annotation.walkthrough: A bower here is someone who bows, a cellist, not a leafy shelter; Pablo Casals was the great Catalan cellist.
annotation.definitionFit: Casals drew his bow across the cello wonderfully, so he was a wonderful bower.

entries.clue: Southern French clan dancing at end of show (9)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged
indicatorNotes.at end of: the rearranged clan comes after the word for show

blocks.note: to show something is to prove it

annotation.surface: A family from the south of France dances as the show closes.
annotation.walkthrough: Show is a verb, to prove, not a performance.
annotation.definitionFit: Provencal describes Provence, in the south of France.

entries.clue: English composer a joy (5)

blocks.note: Sir Arthur, Master of the Queen's Music from 1953

annotation.surface: An English composer who is a delight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A' sits between the halves as a link, making the second half read as praise of the composer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example for the composer, and a plain synonym for joy at its most complete.

entries.clue: Slack lovers finally woke up, but were late for work, probably? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the result; OVERSLEPT is the cause

indicatorNotes.Slack: slack means loose, so the letters are loosened and rearranged
indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of each following word

blocks.note: last letters of woke, up and but

annotation.surface: Lazy lovers woke up at last and were late for the office.
annotation.walkthrough: Slack reads as a description of the lovers but it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who overslept probably arrived late for work.

entries.clue: Another opportunity to see article on pay reforms (6,6)

indicatorNotes.reforms: the letters are formed again in a new order

annotation.surface: A second look at a newspaper piece about pay reforms.
annotation.walkthrough: Article looks like it will give A or THE, but the whole phrase is anagrammed.
annotation.definitionFit: An action replay shows a moment in sport again, another chance to see it.

entries.clue: Store outfit in North London (7)

blocks.note: a store of weapons and ammunition
outfit meaning team: the Premier League football club at the Emirates Stadium

annotation.surface: A shop or kit supplier in north London.
annotation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a football club based in north London; outfit means team.
annotation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons, and Arsenal is a north London football team.

entries.clue: Range of phonetic letters? (6)

annotation.definitionNote: SIERRA is one of the phonetic letters

blocks.note: a mountain range with a jagged, saw-toothed skyline
one of the code words, Alpha to Zulu, used for letters over the radio

annotation.surface: A spread of sounds used in phonetics.
annotation.walkthrough: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet and also a jagged mountain range.
annotation.definitionFit: A sierra is a mountain range, and Sierra is the phonetic code word for S.

entries.clue: Second lecture on my seabird (9)

indicatorNotes.on: the second and lecture come after the word for my

annotation.surface: A moment of lecturing aimed at the speaker's own seabird.
annotation.walkthrough: My is the exclamation of surprise, which COR also is in British speech.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the black diving bird of coasts and estuaries is one kind of seabird.

entries.clue: Worship is embraced by one with benefit (7)

indicatorNotes.embraced by: IS is held inside the other letters

blocks.note: I = one as a Roman numeral

annotation.surface: Worship is welcomed by someone who gains from it.
annotation.walkthrough: The dole is the British term for state unemployment money.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to treat someone as an idol is to worship them, figuratively.

entries.clue: A little titbit, as tempter? (5)

indicatorNotes.A little: only a little of the words is used: the answer is a small piece of them

blocks.note: five letters starting at the last letter of titbit and running into tempter

annotation.surface: A small tasty morsel offered to tempt someone.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue both defines and hides the answer: a taste is a small titbit offered to tempt you.
annotation.definitionFit: A taste is a small sample of food given to tempt you into more.

entries.clue: Vaudeville star, one celebrating? (6)

blocks.note: Sir Harry, the Scottish music-hall singer who toured American vaudeville
one who lauds, heaping praise on something

annotation.surface: A music-hall performer out celebrating.
annotation.walkthrough: Sir Harry Lauder was a Scottish music-hall and vaudeville singer; a lauder is one who lauds.
annotation.definitionFit: One who lauds, or praises, is a lauder, and Harry Lauder was a vaudeville star.

entries.clue: Drink in picnic containers, carbonated? (8)

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon, and carbon-ated read as 'given carbon' adds that symbol
hampers are wicker baskets for picnics

annotation.surface: Fizzy drink packed in the picnic baskets.
annotation.walkthrough: Carbonated reads as fizzy, fitting the drink, but it means 'with carbon added', so C joins the hampers.
annotation.definitionFit: Champers is British slang for champagne, a drink.

entries.clue: Reverend often slipping tongue in kisser (7)

blocks.note: a Victorian Oxford clergyman whose name went to the slip that swaps the starts of words
not the mouth but one who spoons, old slang for canoodling

annotation.surface: A clergyman slips his tongue into someone's mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: The Rev William Spooner gave his name to the spoonerism; kisser is not slang for mouth here but one who spoons, or smooches.
annotation.definitionFit: Spooner was famous for slips of the tongue, and a spooner is someone who spoons, or kisses.

entries.clue: Pretty up on amenable gelding, equestrian initially — in this? (8)

annotation.definition: Pretty up on amenable gelding, equestrian initially — in this?

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, on means placed above, so DRESS comes first
indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of each of the three words before it

blocks.note: to dress is to make pretty
first letters of amenable, gelding, equestrian

annotation.surface: A rider smartened up on a biddable horse: what event is this?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, with 'in this?' pointing to the sport.
annotation.definitionFit: Dressage is the equestrian event where a groomed horse performs precise movements.

entries.clue: Savage lurch, reminder at death in Canterbury tale? (6,2,3,9)

indicatorNotes.Savage: the letters are savaged, torn into a new order

annotation.surface: A violent lurch, a memento mori, all in a story from Canterbury.
annotation.walkthrough: T S Eliot's play is about Thomas Becket's killing in Canterbury Cathedral; Canterbury tale nods at Chaucer as misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: Eliot's play tells of the murder of Becket at Canterbury, so it is a Canterbury tale.

entries.clue: Thus title written upside down underneath the bottle (7)

indicatorNotes.written upside down: in a down clue, upside down reverses the letters
indicatorNotes.underneath: the reversed letters sit below THE

annotation.surface: A heading is printed upside down below the label on a bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: The THE is taken straight from the clue; only SO and MR are reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a vacuum flask, an insulated bottle.

entries.clue: In the dark unable to solve crosswords? (8)

blocks.note: taken literally: without the clues, or unable to crack them

annotation.surface: Someone baffled, who cannot solve crosswords.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition takes clueless literally: without a clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Clueless means ignorant, in the dark, and literally lacking clues.

entries.clue: Heartless relative having dropped in, everybody hiding away (7)

indicatorNotes.having dropped: the relative drops the letters IN
indicatorNotes.hiding away: what is left hides the word for everybody inside it

annotation.surface: An unfeeling relative dropped round while everyone hid.
annotation.walkthrough: Dropped in reads as 'visited', but it tells you to drop the letters IN from COUSIN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word comes from hardened skin, and a person without heart feels nothing for others.

entries.clue: Heat-resistant tiles on spacecraft, vehicle like a rocket (8)

annotation.surface: Tiles on a spacecraft, part of a vehicle that flies like a rocket.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the shuttle's tiles form a hard protective shell.
annotation.definitionFit: A carapace is a hard protective shell, as the heat shield tiles are for a spacecraft.

entries.clue: Turn fan backwards and ventilate after evacuation (7)

indicatorNotes.backwards: the fan's letters are written backwards
indicatorNotes.after evacuation: ventilate is emptied, leaving its outer letters

blocks.note: a fan or lover of something
ventilate with its middle emptied out

annotation.surface: Instructions for a fan: spin it backwards to air a room after it is cleared.
annotation.walkthrough: Fan is a person, an enthusiast, not a machine, despite the ventilating.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a wheel or planet turning about an axis does exactly this.

entries.clue: So long time for hotel employee (5)

annotation.surface: A long shift for someone working in a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: So long reads as a length of time, but it is the goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: A valet is a hotel employee who cleans clothes or parks cars.

entries.clue: Old type-size in collection that’s back in the news (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the type size goes in the collection
indicatorNotes.back: the collection is written back to front

blocks.note: a lot = a collection at auction
pica is an old printing size of 12 point

annotation.surface: An old typeface in a printers' archive that is fashionable again.
annotation.walkthrough: Back in the news looks like a phrase, but back is the reversal signal and in the news is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Something topical is of current interest, in the news.

entries.clue: Obscure winger to arrive in theatre of impossible dreams (5-6-4)

annotation.surface: An unknown footballer arrives at a theatre of dreams.
annotation.walkthrough: Winger and 'theatre of dreams' (Manchester United's nickname for Old Trafford) suggest football; the winger is a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from Aristophanes' Birds: the imaginary city in the sky where hopeless fantasies are played out, their theatre.

entries.clue: Odd pink or blue? (4)

blocks.note: how a steak can be ordered: blue is barely seared, pink lightly cooked

annotation.surface: Something unusual in pink or blue.
annotation.walkthrough: Pink and blue are ways of ordering steak: blue is barely cooked and pink is medium-rare.
annotation.definitionFit: Rare means uncommon, odd, and describes lightly cooked, pink or blue meat.

entries.clue: Mathematical computation, hard stuff (8)

blocks.note: the branch of maths dealing with rates of change, or any system of calculation
a stony deposit, like a kidney stone or tartar on the teeth

annotation.surface: Maths sums are hard going.
annotation.walkthrough: Hard stuff reads as 'difficult material' but means a hard deposit, like tartar on teeth.
annotation.definitionFit: Calculus is a branch of maths and also a hard stony deposit in the body.

entries.clue: Jumbos bit incomplete, defeat admitted (7)

indicatorNotes.incomplete: the bit loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.admitted: the defeat is let in, placed inside

blocks.note: COIN, a bit of money, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Part of the elephants went missing and a defeat was conceded.
annotation.walkthrough: Bit means a coin, as in a threepenny bit.
annotation.definitionFit: Colossi are giants, and jumbo means giant-sized.

entries.clue: Pigment more likely to leak, might you say? (5)

indicatorNotes.might you say: the answer is what you might say, a sound

annotation.surface: A paint that is more prone to running.
annotation.walkthrough: In a British accent, with no final R, seepier and sepia sound alike.
annotation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment originally made from cuttlefish ink.

entries.clue: Drug: one was in possession of the police (9)

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

annotation.surface: A drug case: someone was caught holding it by the police.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces run in reverse clue order: the police (MET) had one.
annotation.definitionFit: Methadone is a drug used to treat heroin addiction.

entries.clue: Change point for old gate (8)

blocks.note: a pike is a spear point

annotation.surface: A place to switch direction at an old gateway.
annotation.walkthrough: A turnpike was the gate on a toll road, opened when the fee was paid.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: the barrier across a toll road, swung open once the fee was paid.

entries.clue: Red label, yet I will appear troubled by design (12)

indicatorNotes.troubled: troubled letters are disturbed into a new order

annotation.surface: A red label troubles someone, who insists it was on purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: Red label sounds like a warning or a whisky, but it is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doing something by design means intending it, not by accident.

entries.clue: Man, male regenerating gradually (9)

indicatorNotes.regenerating: the letters are generated again in a new form

annotation.surface: A man slowly regains his strength, bit by bit.
annotation.walkthrough: Man is a piece in chess or draughts, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means a bit at a time, gradually.

entries.clue: Binds sample embroidery (8)

annotation.surface: A sampler: a piece of stitching bound up.
annotation.walkthrough: A sampler is a piece of embroidery, so sample leans toward the definition while giving TRY.
annotation.definitionFit: Tapestry is a woven or stitched decorative fabric, a kind of embroidery.

entries.clue: Commercials broadcast for bladed tool (4)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: something broadcast is heard, so the answer is a sound

annotation.surface: TV adverts selling a cutting tool.
annotation.walkthrough: Broadcast fits the commercials in the surface; here it signals a sound.
annotation.definitionFit: An adze is a tool with an arched blade used for shaping wood.

entries.clue: Bespoke orders I’m told are covering area (6-4)

indicatorNotes.orders: the letters are put in a new order
indicatorNotes.covering: the rearranged letters cover, or surround, A

annotation.surface: Someone passes on that the custom-made orders cover a whole area.
annotation.walkthrough: I'm told looks like a sound-alike signal, but here it is only anagram fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Savile Row: a bespoke suit is cut to one customer's measurements, as any made-to-measure item is.

entries.clue: Uncommunicative about one being faced by rogue element (7)

indicatorNotes.about: MUM goes about, around, the one

blocks.note: I = one as a Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A silent type is confronted by a rogue character.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition hides at the very end, after the rogue.
annotation.definitionFit: Cadmium is a chemical element, a soft metal.

entries.clue: Childish communication intercepted by supremo? There’s evidence! (9)

indicatorNotes.intercepted by: the answer is caught in the words that follow

blocks.note: nine letters from the last two of supremo to the first of evidence

annotation.surface: A child's message is intercepted by the boss, who crows that it proves something.
annotation.walkthrough: The punctuation breaks the hidden run up, but the letters run on straight through.
annotation.definitionFit: Motherese is baby talk, the way adults speak to small children.

entries.clue: Female and pop party (7)

annotation.surface: A woman and her dad at a party.
annotation.walkthrough: Pop reads as a father, or as pop music, but it is the noise.
annotation.definitionFit: A shebang is a party or affair, as in 'the whole shebang'.

entries.clue: Colour that is used up before blue, warmer? (9)

indicatorNotes.used up: in a down clue, up reverses the letters
indicatorNotes.before: the reversed letters come before blue

annotation.surface: A shade that is used up before a warmer blue.
annotation.walkthrough: Warmer reads as 'more warm', but it is the noun: a thing that warms you in bed.
annotation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt that keeps you warm.

entries.clue: Land unpleasant job, being lab rat (6,3)

blocks.note: Guinea is a country in West Africa
a pig of a job is a nasty one

annotation.surface: Someone gets a grim job as a laboratory rat.
annotation.walkthrough: Land reads as a verb, to secure a job, but it is a country.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for the same thing: both animals stand for any person used as a test subject.

entries.clue: Small change in old cartoon strip? (7)

blocks.note: a trifling sum of money, as in 'working for ...'
Charles Schulz's strip with Charlie Brown and Snoopy, 1950 to 2000

annotation.surface: A small alteration in a vintage comic strip.
annotation.walkthrough: Peanuts is Charles Schulz's strip with Charlie Brown and Snoopy.
annotation.definitionFit: Peanuts means a trifling sum, and it is also a famous comic strip.

entries.clue: Writer inspired by the dream is talking about why our arguments are equally sound? (5,5,5,5)

annotation.definition: why our arguments are equally sound

indicatorNotes.inspired by: the writer is breathed into, placed inside, the other letters
indicatorNotes.about: the fodder is turned about into a new order

blocks.note: ink is what a pen writes with

annotation.surface: A writer moved by 'I have a dream' talks about why both sides are right.
annotation.walkthrough: The dream suggests Martin Luther King, but only its letters are used. INK goes into the anagram after THINK's TH.
annotation.definitionFit: Great minds think alike is said jokingly when two people reach the same view, so both arguments are sound.

entries.clue: French food borne by female messenger (7)

indicatorNotes.borne by: the food is carried inside the female

annotation.surface: A woman courier delivers French food.
annotation.walkthrough: Gabriel is the archangel who brings messages from God.
annotation.definitionFit: The archangel Gabriel is God's messenger in the Bible.

entries.clue: Half-naked, as Alf naked? (7)

blocks.note: read as a person with only the top half bare
read as a man named Alf undressed, but meant as the word 'half' stripped of its top letter

annotation.surface: Someone half-dressed, like a man called Alf with no clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: Alf is HALF with its top letter gone, so it is 'topless' too.
annotation.definitionFit: Topless means naked above the waist, half-naked.

entries.clue: Chance to host first of three contests (6)

indicatorNotes.to host: the chance holds the letter inside it
indicatorNotes.first of: take the first letter of three

blocks.note: evens is an even chance in betting

annotation.surface: A chance to stage the first of three competitions.
annotation.walkthrough: Evens is a bookmaker's term for a fifty-fifty chance.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from sport: each race or competition on an athletics programme is one of these.

entries.clue: Fireball more disastrous, full of energy and temperature (6)

indicatorNotes.disastrous: a disaster wrecks the order of the letters
indicatorNotes.full of: the rearranged letters hold the others inside

annotation.surface: A fireball grows more destructive as it heats with energy.
annotation.walkthrough: A meteor streaking through the sky is a fireball.
annotation.definitionFit: A meteor burning up in the atmosphere is seen as a fireball.

entries.clue: Shudder with terror entering contest (7)

indicatorNotes.entering: the terror goes into the contest

blocks.note: a little terror is a naughty child, a brat

annotation.surface: Someone shakes with fear on entering a competition.
annotation.walkthrough: Terror reads as fear, but it is a naughty child.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs describe a rapid trembling back and forth.

entries.clue: Hit hard, broke (8)

blocks.note: beaten with a leather strap, the old school punishment
short of money, as in '... for cash'

annotation.surface: Something struck hard and smashed.
annotation.walkthrough: Broke means penniless, as in strapped for cash, not smashed.
annotation.definitionFit: Strapped means beaten with a strap, and short of money.

entries.clue: Small muscles, those found on end of nose (5)

annotation.definition: those found on end of nose

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothes labels

annotation.surface: Tiny muscles, such as those at the tip of the nose.
annotation.walkthrough: Specs is short for spectacles, perched on the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: Spectacles often sit on the end of the nose.

entries.clue: Get down from oak originally in tree-lined avenue (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the first letter of oak
indicatorNotes.in: that letter goes in the avenue

blocks.note: a grove is a tree-lined walk or road

annotation.surface: Climbing down from an oak on a leafy avenue.
annotation.walkthrough: Get down means to dance, not to climb out of the tree.
annotation.definitionFit: To groove and to get down both mean to dance with enjoyment.

entries.clue: Rookie shooter (4)

blocks.note: a young male horse, so a novice or newcomer
slang for a gun: Samuel ...'s revolvers, like the .45

annotation.surface: A new recruit with a gun.
annotation.walkthrough: A colt is a young horse, and so a novice; shooter is a gun, the Colt revolver.
annotation.definitionFit: A colt is an inexperienced newcomer, and a Colt is a revolver.

entries.clue: Water thrown back, so wet behind the ears (5)

indicatorNotes.thrown back: the water's letters go back to front

blocks.note: Evian is a brand of mineral water

annotation.surface: Water is thrown over someone, leaving the back of their ears wet.
annotation.walkthrough: Wet behind the ears reads literally after the water, but it means inexperienced.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: like a newborn animal still damp, someone wet behind the ears is inexperienced and unworldly.

entries.clue: Blot that was registered by yours truly on audio? (7)

indicatorNotes.on audio: the answer is heard, a sound

blocks.clueFragment: that was registered by yours truly

annotation.surface: A mark picked up on a recording I made.
annotation.walkthrough: Yours truly means the speaker, I. The sound-alike needs a British accent that drops the R in eyesore.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in 'a blot on the landscape': an ugly thing that spoils the view.

entries.clue: Breed with refined deportment, reportedly? (9)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is spoken, so the answer is a sound

annotation.surface: An elegantly bred animal carrying itself with poise.
annotation.walkthrough: The sound-alike works in a non-rhotic British accent, where proper ends in an 'uh'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used for plants and animals alike: to produce new stock from parents.

entries.clue: When Westminster quietens, that keeps the wet lot on edge (5,6)

indicatorNotes.keeps: the word for that keeps the seas inside it
indicatorNotes.on: that result comes after the edge in an across clue

blocks.note: a sill is a ledge or edge
yon = that, in old or dialect speech
the seas are the wet part of the world

annotation.surface: A time when Parliament goes quiet, which keeps soppy types nervous.
annotation.walkthrough: Westminster is the UK Parliament, whose summer recess leaves papers filling space with trivial stories: the silly season.
annotation.definitionFit: The silly season is late summer, when Parliament is in recess and news is scarce.

entries.clue: Ho hum, pedestrian score checker (5-6)

blocks.note: ho hum is a weary sigh
a pedestrian is one who treads

annotation.surface: A bored, dull person checking the scores in a match.
annotation.walkthrough: Score is a piece of written music, not a result; pedestrian reads as dull but is a walker.
annotation.definitionFit: A sight-reader plays music straight off a score seen for the first time.
